Check that N is a power of two.\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    if (N == 0 || (N & (N - 1)) != 0)\n        throw std::invalid_argument("fft: input size must be a power of two");\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2. The result is stored in `output`.  HPX is used to\n    parallelise the two main phases (bit‑reversal and the butterfly stages).\n\n    Preconditions\n    -------------\n    * `x.size()` must be a power of two (otherwise std::invalid_argument is thrown).\n    * `output` may be empty or have any size – it will be resized to `x.size()`.\n\n    Complexity\n    ----------\n    * O(N log N) arithmetic operations.\n    * O(log N) parallel steps (one HPX `for_loop` per FFT stage).\n\n    Note\n    ----\n    The implementation follows the classic in‑place iterative FFT; the only\n    extra memory used is the `output` vector itself.\n*/\nvoid fft(std::vector<std::complex<double>> const& x,\n         std::vector<std::complex<double>>& output)\n{\n    const std::size_t n = x.size();\n\n    if (n == 0) {\n        output.clear();\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 1.  Verify that n is a power of two.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    if ((n & (n - 1)) != 0)               // not a power of two ?\n        throw std::invalid_argument("fft: input size must be a power of two");\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Prepare the output buffer and perform the bit‑reversed copy.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t log2n = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::log2(n));\n    output.resize(n);\n\n    // Parallel bit‑reversal: each index can be processed independently.\n    hpx::parallel::for_loop(\n        hpx::parallel::execution::par,          // execution policy\n        std::size_t{0}, n,\n        [&](std::size_t i)\n        {\n            // Compute the bit‑reversed index of i.\n            std::size_t rev = 0;\n            for (std::size_t b = 0; b < log2n; ++b)\n                if (i & (std::size_t{1} << b))\n                    rev |= std::size_t{1} << (log2n - 1 - b);\n\n            output[rev] = x[i];\n        });\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3.  Iterative butterfly stages.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const double two_pi = 2.0 * M_PI;\n\n    for (std::size_t s = 1; s <= log2n; ++s)          // stage number\n    {\n        const std::size_t m   = std::size_t{1} << s; // FFT length of this stage\n        const std::size_t m2  = m >> 1;               // half‑size\n        const double      theta = -two_pi / static_cast<double>(m);\n        const std::complex<double> wm = std::exp(std::complex<double>(0.0, theta));\n\n        // Each block of size `m` is independent → parallelise over the block start.\n        hpx::parallel::for_loop(\n            hpx::parallel::execution::par,\n            std::size_t{0}, n, m,\n            [&](std::size_t k)               // k = start index of the block\n            {\n                std::complex<double> w = 1.0;\n                for (std::size_t j = 0; The result is written into `output`.\n    The routine assumes that `x.size()` is a power of two; if it is not,\n    the behaviour is undefined (the caller may pad the input).\n\n    The implementation is fully parallelised with HPX:\n      • the bit‑reversal permutation is performed with a parallel for‑loop,\n      • each FFT stage (butterfly) is executed with a parallel for‑loop\n        over the independent “butterfly groups”.\n    No auxiliary helper functions are used – everything lives inside this\n    function body, as requested.\n*/\nvoid fft(std::vector<std::complex<double>> const& x,\n         std::vector<std::complex<double>>& output)\n{\n    const std::size_t N = x.size();\n    if (N == 0) return; Basic sanity checks\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    if (N == 0)\n        throw std::invalid_argument("fft: input size must be > 0");\n\n    // radix‑2 requires a power‑of‑two length\n    if ((N & (N - 1)) != 0)\n        throw std::invalid_argument("fft: input size must be a power of two");\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2. By spawning the two recursive\ncalls as separate HPX tasks we obtain a **task‑parallel** FFT that scales\nwell on many cores while keeping the algorithmic complexity `O(N log N)`.\n\nThe implementation below\n\n* lives completely inside the single function `fft` (no external helper\n  functions);\n* uses a small **cut‑off** (`min_parallel`) – below this size the recursion is\n  performed sequentially to avoid the overhead of creating too many tiny tasks;\n* works for any power‑of‑two length (the classic requirement for radix‑2 FFT);\n* returns the result in the user‑provided `output` vector;\n* assumes HPX has already been started (the program is compiled with\n  `hpx_main.hpp` as in the skeleton).\n\n```cpp\n#include <hpx/hpx_main.hpp>\n#include <hpx/include/async.hpp>\n#include <hpx/include/lcos.hpp>\n#include <complex>\n#include <vector>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <functional>\n\n/*  Compute the discrete Fourier transform of x (radix‑2 Cooley‑Tukey).\n    The result is stored in \'output\'.  The routine is fully parallelised\n    with HPX tasks and contains no external helper functions.                     */\nvoid fft(std::vector<std::complex<double>> const& x,\n         std::vector<std::complex<double>>&       output)\n{\n    const std::size_t N = x.size();\n    output.clear();\n    if (N == 0) return;   // 4096 elements\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2)  Recursive lambda that works in‑place on a buffer.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------\n    std::function<void(std::vector<std::complex<double>>&,\n                       std::size_t)> fft_rec;\n\n    fft_rec = [&](std::vector<std::complex<double>>& buf,\n                  std::size_t n)\n    {\n        if (n == 1) return;                 // base case – already a 1‑point DFT\n\n        const std::size_t half = n / 2;\n\n        // split the current buffer into even and odd parts\n        std::vector<std::complex<double>> even(half);\n        std::vector<std::complex<double>> odd (half);\n        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < half; ++i)\n        {\n            even[i] = buf[2*i];\n            odd[i]  = buf[2*i + 1];\n        }\n\n        // ----------------------------------------------------------\n        // 3)  Parallel recursion – spawn two HPX tasks when the size\n        //     justifies it.\n        // ----------------------------------------------------------\n        hpx::future<void> f_even, f_odd;\n        if (n >= min_parallel)\n        {\n            f_even = hpx::async(fft_rec, std::ref(even), half);\n            f_odd  = hpx::async(fft_rec, std::ref(odd ), half);\n            hpx::wait_all(f_even, f_odd);\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            fft_rec(even, half);\n            fft_rec(odd , half);\n        }\n\n        // ----------------------------------------------------------\n        // 4)  Combine the two half‑size transforms.\n        // ----------------------------------------------------------\n        const double two_pi = 2.0 * std::acos(-1.0);\n        for (std::size_t k = 0; k < half; ++k)\n        {\n            // twiddle factor  exp(-2π i k / n)\n            const double angle = -two_pi * static_cast<double>(k) / static_cast<double>(n);\n            const std::complex<double> twiddle = std::polar(1.0, angle);\n\n            const std::complex<double> t = twiddle * odd[k];\n            buf[k]        = even[k] + t;
